smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Find the height first
smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let $O$ be the center of $\omega$ and $D$ the point where $AB$ touches $\omega$. Then $OD=1$ and $\angle OAD=30^\circ$ (the tangent from $A$ makes $30^\circ$ with line $AM$, where $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, because $AB$ makes $30^\circ$ with $AM$ in the equilateral triangle). So $\triangle ADO$ is $30$-$60$-$90$ and $OA=2$. Since $OM=1$ (tangency at $M$, with $O$ on the opposite side of $BC$ from $A$), $AM=OA-OM=1$.

The height of the equilateral triangle is $1$, so its side is $\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=\frac{2\sqrt3}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}$**

smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Law of Cosines
smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
With $BC=l$: $AC^2=AB^2+l^2-2\cdot AB\cdot l\cos30^\circ$, so $4=9+l^2-3\sqrt3\,l$, i.e. $l^2-3\sqrt3\,l+5=0$. The roots are $l=\frac{3\sqrt3\pm\sqrt7}{2}$ (the ambiguous case of SSA).

Then $\frac{l_2}{l_1}=\frac{3\sqrt3+\sqrt7}{3\sqrt3-\sqrt7}=\frac{(3\sqrt3+\sqrt7)^2}{27-7}=\frac{34+6\sqrt{21}}{20}=\frac{17+3\sqrt{21}}{10}$.

**Answer: $\frac{17+3\sqrt{21}}{10}$**

smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Butterfly theorem and heights
smt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
The line $DE$ (the perpendicular bisector of $BC$) passes through the center of the circle, so it is a diameter and is perpendicular to the line through $F$ parallel to $BC$; hence $F$ is the midpoint of the chord of $\Omega$ cut out by that line. The chords $AD$ and $CE$ cross this chord at $G$ and $H$ (a butterfly configuration), so by the Butterfly Theorem $F$ is the midpoint of $GH$: $FG=FH$.

Triangles $CHF$ and $DGF$ therefore have equal bases ($FH=FG$) on the line $GH$, and their heights over this line are $FM$ (for $C$, which is at the same height as $M$) and $FD$ (for $D$). So $\frac{[CHF]}{[DGF]}=\frac{FM}{FD}$.

Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. $FM=\frac12BC\tan C$ and, since $\angle MCD=\frac A2$, $MD=\frac12BC\tan\frac A2$. With $\cos A=\frac{25+49-64}{70}=\frac17$ and $\cos C=\frac{49+64-25}{112}=\frac{11}{14}$: $\tan\frac A2=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\tan C=\frac{5\sqrt3}{11}$.

The ratio is $\frac{FM}{FM+MD}=\frac{5\sqrt3/11}{5\sqrt3/11+\sqrt3/2}=\frac{10}{10+11}=\frac{10}{21}$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{21}$**
